messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Why do long-running software systems become harder to change over time, even when every individual change was reviewed, tested, and locally correct?

Stay within this direction: Semantic entropy of identifiers and interfaces increases monotonically due to non-colliding name reuse

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Every locally correct change that reuses an existing identifier or interface name for a semantically distinct purpose increases the global semantic entropy of the codebase, because the absence of an immediate name collision allows the change to pass review and tests. Over time, this non-colliding name reuse accumulates monotonically, causing each identifier to carry an expanding distribution of contextual meanings. Consequently, the expected cost of any future change rises as developers must disambiguate an ever-growing set of implicit semantic intents attached to the same names, making the system progressively harder to modify even though no single change introduced a defect."}
